sections.html:
Newberg is a Yamhill County city on the west bank of the Willamette River, about 25 miles southwest of Portland along Oregon Route 99W. It lies within the Portland metropolitan area and covers roughly 6 square miles.

Springbrook, once a separate community, is now part of the city. George Fox University sits in the city center, so the campus is part of the core neighborhoods that surround downtown.

Newberg grew from fur-trade and Quaker roots. Trader Ewing Young settled near Chehalem Creek in 1834, and Joseph Rogers settled the townsite in 1848, so the place was first called Chehalem and then Roger's Landing.

  • The town was platted in 1883 and incorporated in 1889.
  • Tradition says first postmaster Sebastian Brutscher named it for his former hometown of Neuberg, Germany.
  • The Newberg Graphic, the oldest surviving local paper, started December 1, 1888.
  • Quakers founded Friends Pacific Academy in 1885. It became Pacific College in 1891 and George Fox University in 1949.
  • Herbert Hoover came to Newberg in 1885 to live with his uncle and aunt, and the Hoover-Minthorn House is now a museum.

Newberg grew from 514 residents in 1890 to more than 26,000 today, and it is the second most populous city in Yamhill County. The Census Bureau estimates 26,896 residents as of July 1, 2025.

In 2020, 9,005 households lived in the city and 61.3% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. The median age was 35.2.

sections.h2: What employers shape the Newberg economy?
sections.html:
Education, health care, manufacturing and hospitality make up the local base. George Fox University and Providence Newberg Medical Center are named among the city's major employers.

  • A-dec, a dental equipment maker, was the largest employer as of 2002, with 832 employees. George Fox had 400.
  • The Allison Inn and Spa opened in September 2009 with 77 rooms and about 200 full-time workers.
  • A Hazelden Betty Ford inpatient addiction treatment center operates in the city.
  • WestRock owns the former White Birch paper facility in Newberg.
  • Portland Community College opened a campus here in 2011.

Commuters typically continue north on 99W toward Portland, so highway access is part of how a Newberg address gets described.

sections.h2: What is Newberg's climate and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Newberg has cool, wet winters and warm, dry summers. July is the warmest month with an average high of 80.0 degrees, while December and January highs average 46.

Rain averages 39.95 inches a year over about 152 days. Freezing temperatures occur on about 33 nights a year, with snow mainly from December through March. The record high is 107 degrees and the record low is minus 3. Water in crawl spaces, gutters that overflow, and pipes in unheated areas are the usual trouble spots for older houses here.

sections.h2: How do highways and the bypass affect Newberg buyers?
sections.html:
Oregon Route 99W runs east to west through Newberg, linking Portland to the northeast with Dundee and McMinnville to the southwest. For years that single road carried severe congestion through the Newberg-Dundee area.

The Newberg-Dundee Bypass was built to relieve it. Phase 1, a four-mile road with one lane each way from OR 219 to OR 99W south of Dundee, opened January 6, 2018. The full bypass is planned at 11 miles and a four-lane expressway, but funding so far covers Phase 1 and design of Phase 2, per the Oregon Department of Transportation. Freight moves on the Portland & Western Railroad, and regular passenger rail ended in the 1930s.

Newberg-Dundee Public Schools runs six elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, Newberg High School and Catalyst Alternative High School. Private Christian schools include Veritas School and C. S. Lewis Academy.

George Fox University is classed by U.S. News & World Report as a first-tier regional university, and Portland Community College runs a campus in the city.

sections.h2: How does Yamhill County assess property for a Newberg house?
sections.html:
Yamhill County values and bills Newberg property under rules set by state law. Under ORS 308.146, taxable value is the lesser of market value and a maximum assessed value that normally rises no more than 3% a year.

That cap resets when a property is new, rebuilt or substantially altered, so a house you improved or a lot that was split may be assessed differently. Taxes are due in three parts, on November 15, February 15 and May 15. A 3% discount applies to a full payment made by November 15. Ask your title company to prorate the bill at closing. Interest of 1 1/3% per month applies to late amounts, so confirm early whether any installment is still unpaid.

sections.h2: What about a Newberg house that is part of an estate?
sections.html:
Sales by court-appointed personal representatives and trustees are excluded from Oregon's seller disclosure rules under ORS 105.470. So are sales by a financial institution that took the property through foreclosure.

Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes must provide a signed disclosure statement to each buyer who makes a written offer. If a buyer gets one, they have five business days to revoke unless they signed a waiver. Getting the right paperwork lined up first keeps an inherited sale from stalling.

sections.h2: How does Newberg fit into Yamhill County?
sections.html:
Newberg shares Yamhill County with McMinnville, Lafayette and Sheridan. The county covers 718 square miles, counted 107,722 residents in 2020, and is the fifth-smallest county in Oregon by area.

Wine is a large part of the county economy. Yamhill has more vineyard acreage than any other Oregon county, with over 80 wineries and six American Viticultural Areas wholly or partly inside its borders. Logging remains the mainstay of the western part of the county. A Newberg seller with acreage or a rural lot should ask which tax and land-use rules apply before pricing it.

sections.h2: What do Newberg sellers usually compare?
sections.html:
• Listing with an agent versus accepting an as-is offer from a cash buyer.
  • Repair costs on an older house versus selling in present condition.
  • Closing date, tax proration and utility transfers.
  • Whether a tenant or a college renter is in the house.
  • Whether the lot is inside city limits, since city and county rules differ for rural parcels in Yamhill County.

Each buyer sets its own terms, so ask for them in writing before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is Newberg, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Newberg is in Yamhill County, in the Portland metropolitan area. McMinnville is the county seat, and Newberg is the second most populous city in the county.

faqs.q: How many people live in Newberg?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 26,896 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,138 in the 2020 census.
It is a planned 11-mile expressway on OR 18 meant to ease congestion on OR 99W. Phase 1, four miles, opened January 6, 2018.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Newberg house?
faqs.a: November 15, February 15 and May 15. Full payment by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and two-thirds paid by then earns 2%.

faqs.q: Do I need a disclosure statement if I sell an inherited house in Newberg?
faqs.a: Not if a court-appointed personal representative or trustee is the seller, since ORS 105.470 excludes those sales. Other sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must provide one.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Newberg?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied homes is $472,100. That is a city-wide median and not a price for any one house.
